rationale: Recurring noun for cosmic combat (lines 6, 9, 16, 21, 27). Stands in synonymous parallel with ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ (line 10) and the entity is consistently the war from which the First Man returns. Likely Lycopolitan or specifically Manichaean lexeme; not in standard Coptic lexica.

Greek loanword χειροτονία — formal investiture by hand-imposition. Used here of the Mother of Life's act commissioning the First Man for the cosmic battle (parallel verb ⲭⲉⲗⲣⲟⲧⲟⲛⲓ in line 5). Standard ecclesiastical-investiture term repurposed cosmologically.

proposed_english: to arm fully / equip with full panoply
rationale: Greek loanword πανοπλίζω 'to arm with full armor.' Captures the martial-investiture imagery: the Mother arms the First Man head-to-foot before sending him into the cosmic battle.

Lycopolitan ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call, summon, invite' as nominal/agentive. Functions on this page as a divine entity who 'gives' peace to the First Man and 'sends him forth from the Father.' Same root as previously attested ⲧⲁⲍⲙ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'summon forth.'

Lycopolitan ⲙⲉϩ-ⲥⲛⲉⲩ/ⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'second' (m./f.). Used iteratively across this page to label each successive mystery's earthly counterpart — possibly meaning 'the second instance' (i.e. the earthly enactment) of each mystery's heavenly archetype.
ⲛⲉϩⲣⲱⲙⲉ = Lycopolitan plural with epenthetic ϩ (cf. ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ). The 'house of the men' = the kingdom of the First Man and his Five Sons in the realm of Light. Cosmological-architectural term.

proposed_english: go on a journey / travel abroad
rationale: Greek loanword ἀποδημέω 'to be away from home, travel abroad.' Standard NT lexeme retained in Coptic for distant travel.
